title: Census on Foreign Liabilities and Assets of Indian Direct Investment Entities for 2025-26
file_extracted_text:
November 06, 2026 
 
Census on Foreign Liabilities and Assets of Indian Direct Investment Entities for 
2025-26  
     Today, the Reserve Bank released the provisional results of the 2025-261 round of the 
annual census on foreign liabilities and assets (FLA) covering cross-border liabilities and 
assets of the Indian entities [viz., companies, limited liability partnerships (LLPs), 
alternative investment funds (AIFs) and partnership firms] with inward/outward direct 
investment. The FLA census captures detailed information on foreign liabilities and assets 
in terms of direct investment, portfolio investment and other investments comprising of 
trade credit, loans, currency & deposits and other payables and receivables accounts, 
activity sector, sales, purchase, exports, and imports. The variations in outstanding foreign 
assets / liabilities between the beginning and end of a financial year would be different from 
flows recorded in India’s balance of payments (BoP) statistics during the year, as the 
former would also include valuation changes due to price and exchange rate movements. 
 
Key highlights: 
 
• Of the total number of Indian entities reporting foreign direct investment (FDI) and/or 
overseas direct investment (ODI), around 97 per cent entities were unlisted as at end-
March 2026, and also held a major share in total FDI equity capital (at face value) in 
India (Tables 1 and 2A).  
 
• Non-financial companies accounted for more than 90 per cent of the FDI equity at face 
value (Table 2B). 
 
• In terms of market value, listed and unlisted companies had almost equal share in total 
FDI equity capital as at end-March 2026, however, 96.6 per cent of the FDI debt is held 
by unlisted companies (Table 3A). 
 
• In rupee terms, the ratio of inward FDI to ODI moderated to 4.2 times as on end-March 
2026 from 5.5 times a year ago (Table 3B). 
 
• Other investment liabilities [viz., trade credit, loans, currency and deposits, and other 
payables with unrelated (third party) non-resident entities] recorded a growth of 11.9 per 
cent (y-o-y) in rupee terms as on end-March 2026; other investment assets with 
unrelated non-residents also rose by 16.1 per cent during the same period (Table 4). 
 
  
 
1 The previous data release in the series, covering 2024-25 census round, was published on October 29, 
2025, on the RBI website.

• The United States of America (16.5 per cent) followed by Mauritius (14.5 per cent),

States of America were the top destinations together accounting for more than 50 per 
cent share (Tables 5 and 6). 
 
• Manufacturing sector accounted for the highest share in the total outstanding FDI equity 
capital at market value (50.1 per cent), while 45 per cent share was held by services 
sector (Tables 7 and 8).

title: Sectoral Deployment of Credit by NBFC – September 2026
file_extracted_text:
November 06, 2026 
 
Sectoral Deployment of Credit by NBFC – September 2026 
     Data on sectoral deployment of credit by non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) 
for the month of September 2026, collected from major NBFCs and housing finance 
companies (HFCs), are set out in the Statement1.  
     On a year-on-year (y-o-y) basis, NBFCs’ credit registered a growth of 15.4 per cent in 
September 2026 as compared to 13.3 per cent a year ago. 
Highlights of the sectoral deployment of credit by NBFCs for the month ended 
September 30, 2026, are given below: 
• 
Credit to agriculture and allied activities recorded a robust growth of 17.8 per cent 
(y-o-y) in September 2026 as against 5.2 per cent a year ago. 
 
• 
Credit growth in industry sector declined to 7.4 per cent (y-o-y) in September 2026 
as compared with 10.2 per cent in September 2025. Within industry, credit growth 
in ‘infrastructure’ remained subdued. 
 
• 
Credit growth in services sector moderated to 17.3 per cent (y-o-y) in September 
2026 from 23.0 per cent a year ago. While credit to ‘commercial real estate’ 
marked buoyant expansion, ‘trade’ and ‘transport operators’ segments also witnessed 
higher credit growth.  
 
• 
Retail loans growth accelerated to 21.9 per cent (y-o-y) in September 2026 
compared to 16.8 per cent a year ago. Within retail sector, ‘housing loans’, ‘loans 
against gold jewellery’ and ‘vehicle loans’ witnessed accelerated credit growth. 
 
 
 
 
                                                                                                               Ajit Prasad

HFCs, accounting for about 87 per cent of total credit with respect to data published in ‘Report on Trend and Progress of Banking in India 2024-25’ (RTP 2024-25, 
outstanding as on September 2025).

November 06, 2026 
 
Directions under Section 35A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation 
Act, 1949 – Sri Guru Raghavendra Sahakara Bank Niyamitha, Bengaluru - 
Extension of Period 
     The Reserve Bank of India issued Directions under Section 35A read with Section 
56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 to Sri Guru Raghavendra Sahakara Bank 
Niyamitha, Bengaluru vide Directive No. DoS.CO.UCB.BSD-III.D-2/12.23.283/2019-
20 dated January 02, 2020, for a period of six months up to close of business on July 
10, 2020. The Reserve Bank of India is satisfied that in the public interest, it is 
necessary to further extend the period of operation of the Directive beyond close of 
business on November 10, 2026. 
2. Accordingly, the Reserve Bank of India, in the exercise of powers vested in it under 
sub-section (1) of Section 35A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 
1949, hereby extends the Directive for a further period of six months from close of 
business on November 10, 2026 to close of business on May 10, 2027, subject to 
review. 
3. The aforesaid extension and /or modification by the Reserve Bank of India should 
not per-se be construed to imply that the Reserve Bank of India is satisfied with the 
financial position of the bank. 
4. Other terms and conditions of the Directive under reference, shall remain 
unchanged.

the ‘Scheme for Non-competitive Bidding Facility’. Individual investors can also place bids as per 
the non-competitive scheme through the Retail Direct portal (https://rbiretaildirect.org.in). 
     Both competitive and non-competitive bids for the auction should be submitted in electronic 
format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (E-Kuber) system on November 09, 
2026 (Monday). The competitive bids should be submitted between 10:30 A.M. and 11:30 
A.M. and non-competitive bids should be submitted between 10:30 A.M. and 11:00 A.M.  
     In case of technical difficulties, Core Banking Operations Team may be contacted (email; 
Phone no: 022-69870466, 022-69870415). 
     For other auction related difficulties, IDMD Auction Team can be contacted (email; Phone no: 
022-22702431, 022-22705125).  
     Only in the event of system failure, physical bids would be accepted. Such physical bids should 
be submitted to the Public Debt Office (email; Phone no: 022-22603456, 022-22603457, 022-

     The yield per cent per annum or the price as the case may be, expected by the bidder should 
be expressed up to two decimal points. An investor can submit more than one competitive bid at 
same/different rates of yield or prices in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core 
Banking Solution (E-Kuber) system. However, the aggregate amount of bids submitted by a bidder 
should not exceed the notified amount for each State. 
     The Reserve Bank of India will determine the maximum yield / minimum price at which bids will 
be accepted. Stock will be issued for a minimum nominal amount of ₹10,000.00 and in multiples of 
₹10,000.00 thereafter. 
     The results of the auction will be announced on November 09, 2026 (Monday) and payment 
by successful bidders will be made during banking hours on November 11, 2026 (Wednesday) at 
Mumbai and at respective Regional Offices of RBI. 
     The new State Government Stocks will bear interest at the rates determined by RBI at the 
auctions. For the new stock, interest will be paid half yearly on May 11 and November 11 of each 
year till maturity. For the re-issued Government Stock, interest will be paid at the rate as 
determined on the date of original issue of Government Stock and will be paid on half yearly basis 
till maturity. The Stocks will be governed by the provisions of the Government Securities Act, 2006 
and the Government Securities Regulations, 2007. 
     The investment in State Government Stocks will be reckoned as an eligible investment in 
Government Securities by banks for the purpose of Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) under Section 
24 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949. The stocks will qualify for the ready forward facility.

file_extracted_text:
November 05, 2026 
 
Consolidation of Instructions Related to Priority Sector Lending – Drafts for 
Comments 
 
     As part of the ongoing effort towards consolidation of various instructions issued 
from time to time, the Reserve Bank has undertaken a review of the extant guidelines 
relating to Priority Sector Lending (PSL) and proposes to issue Directions on the 
subject RE-wise. 
 
2. Accordingly, the following draft Directions are being placed on the website for 
public comments: 
 
a) Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Priority Sector Lending – Targets 
and Classification) Directions, 2026 
b) Reserve Bank of India (Small Finance Banks – Priority Sector Lending – 
Targets and Classification) Directions, 2026 
c) Reserve Bank of India (Local Area Banks – Priority Sector Lending – Targets 
and Classification) Directions, 2026 
d) Reserve Bank of India (Regional Rural Banks – Priority Sector Lending – 
Targets and Classification) Directions, 2026 
e) Reserve Bank of India (Urban Co-operative Banks – Priority Sector Lending – 
Targets and Classification) Directions, 2026 
3. Further, instructions which have not been included in the consolidated draft 
Directions would be repealed consequent to the issuance of the Directions. The 
same will be notified separately.  
 
4. The comments / feedback may be submitted on or before November 26, 2026, 
through the following channels: 
 
i. 
The ‘Connect 2 Regulate’ section on the website by following the 
corresponding hyperlink provided against each document in the page where 
they are hosted. 
or 
 
ii. 
by e-mail with the subject line ‘Feedback on [full name of the draft Direction / 
(including the type of Regulated Entity)]’.

November 05, 2026 
 
Directions under Section 35A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation 
Act, 1949 – The Pusad Urban Co-operative Bank Ltd., Pusad, Dist. Yavatmal,  
Maharashtra – Extension of Period 
 
     The Reserve Bank of India issued Directions under Section 35A read with Section 
56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 to The Pusad Urban Co-operative Bank Ltd., 
Pusad, Dist. Yavatmal, Maharashtra vide Directive No. NGP.DOS.SSM3.No.S611/5-
04-166/2025-2026 dated November 06, 2025,  for a period of six months up to close 
of business on May 07, 2026, which was last extended up to the close of business on 
November 07, 2026, vide Directive No. DOR.MON/D-30/12-22-635/2026-27 dated 
July 31, 2026. The Reserve Bank of India is satisfied that in the public interest, it is 
necessary to further extend the period of operation of the Directive beyond close of 
business on November 07, 2026.  
 
2. Accordingly, the Reserve Bank of India, in the exercise of powers vested in it under 
sub-section (1) of Section 35A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 
1949, hereby extends the Directive for a further period of three months from close of 
business on November 07, 2026, to close of business on February 07, 2027, subject 
to review.  
 
3. The aforesaid extension and /or modification by the Reserve Bank of India should 
not per se be construed to imply that the Reserve Bank of India is satisfied with the 
financial position of the bank.  
 
4. Other terms and conditions of the Directive under reference, shall remain 
unchanged.

title: Constitution of the Technical Consultative Committee for Financial Markets (TCCFM)
file_extracted_text:
November 04, 2026 
 
Constitution of the Technical Consultative Committee for Financial 
Markets (TCCFM) 
 
     In pursuance of the announcement made in the Statement on Developmental and 
Regulatory Policies dated October 7, 2026, the Reserve Bank of India announces the 
constitution of the Technical Consultative Committee for Financial Markets (TCCFM) 
against the backdrop of rapidly evolving financial markets and infrastructure. The 
Committee will serve as a forum for structured engagement with market participants 
and stakeholders by the Reserve Bank on policy and operational matters related to 
money, government securities and foreign exchange markets as well as the respective 
derivative markets and infrastructure. 
 
2. The Committee will be Chaired by the Deputy Governor (DG) in charge of the 
Financial Markets Regulation Department (FMRD) of the Reserve Bank of India. The 
Committee will comprise the following external members: 
 
i. 
Shri Ananth Narayan, Former Whole Time Member, SEBI, and Professor 
of Practice, IIT Bombay;  
ii. 
Shri Shamsher Singh, Chairman, Fixed Income Money Market and 
Derivatives Association of India (FIMMDA) and Deputy Managing Director, 
State Bank of India; 
iii. 
Shri Neeraj Gambhir, Executive Director, Axis Bank;  
iv. 
Shri Shailendra Jhingan, Head, Treasury and Economic Research, ICICI 
Bank; 
v. 
Shri Aditya Bagree, Managing Director, Head (Markets), Citibank India; 
vi. 
Shri Nand Kishore, Managing Director, Clearing Corporation of India 
Limited; and  
vii. 
Shri Ridham Desai, Managing Director, Morgan Stanley India. 
 
3. The Terms of Reference (ToR) of the Technical Consultative Committee for 
Financial Markets will be as under: 
 
i. 
Issues related to the functioning, efficiency, liquidity and resilience of the 
money, government securities, foreign exchange and related derivative 
markets, and identification of measures to deepen and broaden these 
markets. 
ii. 
Issues relating to trading, clearing, settlement, reporting and other market 
infrastructure, including the associated regulatory and operational 
frameworks. 
iii. 
Emerging policy and operational issues affecting financial markets, 
including implementation of RBI measures and identification of unintended 
market frictions.

title: RBI launches the November 2026 round of the Rural Consumer Confidence Survey
file_extracted_text:
November 03, 2026 
 
RBI launches the November 2026 round of the Rural Consumer Confidence Survey 
 
     The Reserve Bank of India has been regularly conducting Rural Consumer 
Confidence Survey (RCCS). The November 2026 round of the survey is being launched. 
The survey collects current perceptions and one year ahead expectations of households 
on general economic situation, employment scenario, overall price situation, own income 
and spending from the households residing in the rural and semi-urban areas across 31 
states/ UTs viz., Andhra Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Goa, 
Gujarat, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Jharkhand, Karnataka, 
Keralam, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, NCT 
of Delhi, Odisha, Punjab, Rajasthan, Sikkim, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Tripura, Union 
Territory of Ladakh, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and West Bengal. The results of this 
survey provide useful inputs for monetary policy. 
 
     The agency, Ipsos Research Private Ltd., Gurugram has been engaged to conduct 
the survey of this round on behalf of the Reserve Bank of India. For this purpose, the 
selected households will be approached by the agency, and they are requested to 
provide their response. Other individuals, who are not approached by the agency can 
also participate in this survey by providing their responses using the linked survey 
schedule. The filled in survey schedule may be e-mailed as per contact details given 
below. In case of any query/clarification, kindly contact at the following address: 
 
The Director, 
Division of Household Surveys, 
Department of Statistics and Information Management,

C-8, 2nd Floor,

Mumbai-400 051; 
Phone: 022-2657 8398, 022-2657 8332; 
Please click here to send email.

title: RBI launches the November 2026 round of the Inflation Expectations Survey of Households
file_extracted_text:
November 03, 2026 
 
RBI launches the November 2026 round of the Inflation Expectations Survey of 
Households 
 
     The Reserve Bank of India has been regularly conducting Inflation Expectations 
Survey of Households (IESH). The November 2026 round of the survey is being 
launched. The survey aims at capturing subjective assessments on price movements and 
inflation, based on their individual consumption baskets, across 19 cities, viz., 
Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Bhopal, Bhubaneswar, Chandigarh, Chennai, Delhi, Guwahati, 
Hyderabad, Jaipur, Jammu, Kolkata, Lucknow, Mumbai, Nagpur, Patna, Raipur, Ranchi 
and Thiruvananthapuram. The survey seeks qualitative responses from households on 
price changes (general prices as well as prices of specific product groups) in the three 
months ahead as well as in the one year ahead period and quantitative responses on 
current, three months ahead and one year ahead inflation rates. The results of this 
survey provide useful inputs for monetary policy. 
 
     The agency, M/s Hansa Research Group Pvt. Ltd., Mumbai has been engaged to 
conduct the survey of this round on behalf of the Reserve Bank of India. For this purpose, 
the selected households will be approached by the agency, and they are requested to 
provide their response. Other individuals, who are not approached by the agency can 
also participate in this survey by providing their responses using the linked survey 
schedule. The filled in survey schedule may be e-mailed as per contact details given

3. The securities will be sold through Reserve Bank of India Mumbai Office, Fort, Mumbai – 
400001. The sale will be subject to the terms and conditions spelt out in the ‘Specific 
Notification’ mentioned above and the General Notification F.No.4(2)–B(W&M)/2018, dated 
March 26, 2025. 
 
4. The auction will be conducted using multiple price method. Both competitive and non-
competitive bids for the auction should be submitted in electronic format on the Reserve Bank 
of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system) on November 06, 2026 (Friday). The non-
competitive bids should be submitted between 10:30 a.m. and 11:00 a.m. and the 
competitive bids should be submitted between 10:30 a.m. and 11:30 a.m. The result will be 
announced on the same day and payment by successful bidders will have to be made on 
November 09, 2026 (Monday). 
 
5. Bids for underwriting of the Additional Competitive Underwriting (ACU) portion can be 
submitted by ‘Primary Dealers’ from 09:00 a.m. up to 09:30 a.m. on November 06, 2026 
(Friday) on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system). 
 
6. The securities will be eligible for “When Issued” trading for a period commencing from                        
November 03, 2026 – November 06, 2026. 
 
7. Operational guidelines for Government of India dated securities auction and other details 
are given in the Annex. 
 
                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                   Ajit Prasad

प्रेस प्रकाशनी PRESS RELEASE 
 
 
  
भारतीय ǐरज़वर् बैंक 
 
RESERVE BANK OF INDIA 
 
  वेबसाइट : www.rbi.org.in/hindi 
संचार ͪ वभाग, केंद्रȣय कायार्लय, शहȣद भगत ͧ संह मागर्, फोटर्, मुंबई - 400 001 
Website : www.rbi.org.in 
Department of Communication, Central Office, Shahid Bhagat Singh Marg, Fort,  
ई-मेल/email : helpdoc@rbi.org.in 
Mumbai - 400 001 फोन/Phone: 022 - 2266 0502 
 
ANNEX 
Type of Auction 
 
1. For multiple price-based auction, successful bids will get accepted at the respective quoted 
yield/price for the security. For uniform price-based auction, bids will get accepted at the cut 
off yield/price accepted in the auction.  
 
2. The auction will be yield based for new security and price based for securities which are 
re-issued.  
 
3. In case of a Floating Rate Bonds (FRB), the auction will be spread-based for new security 
and price based for securities which are reissued. At the time of placing bids for new FRB, 
the spread should be quoted in percentage terms.  
 
Minimum Bid Size 
 
4. The securities will be issued for a minimum amount of ₹10,000/- (nominal) and in multiples 
of ₹10,000/- thereafter. 
   
Non-Competitive Segment 
 
5. In all the auctions, Government security up to 5% of the notified amount for sale of individual 
security will be allotted to the eligible individuals and institutions under the Scheme for Non-
competitive Bidding Facility in the Auctions of Government Securities. Individual investors 
can also place bids as per the non-competitive scheme through the Retail Direct portal 
(https://rbiretaildirect.org.in). 
 
6. Each bank or Primary Dealer (PD) on the basis of firm orders received from their constituents 
will submit a single consolidated non-competitive bid for individual security on behalf of its 
constituents in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-
Kuber system).  
 
7. Allotment under the non-competitive segment will be at the weighted average rate of 
yield/price of the successful bids that will emerge in the auction on the basis of the 
competitive bidding. 
 
Submission of Bids 
 
8. Both competitive and non-competitive bids for the auction should be submitted in electronic 
format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).  
 
9. Bids in physical form will not be accepted except in extraordinary circumstances.  
 
Business Continuity Plan (BCP)-IT failure 
 
10. Only in the event of system failure, physical bids will be accepted. Such physical bids should 
be submitted to the Public Debt Office, Mumbai through (email; Phone no: 022-22603456, 
022-22603457, 022-22603190) in the prescribed form which can be obtained from RBI 
website (https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewForms.aspx) before the auction timing ends.  
 
11. In case of technical difficulties, Core Banking Operations Team should be contacted (email; 
Phone no: 022-69870466, 022-69870415). 
 
12. For other auction related difficulties, IDMD auction team can be contacted (email; Phone no: 
022-22702431, 022-22705125). 
 
 
 
 
Multiple Bids 
 
13. An investor can submit more than one competitive bid in electronic format on the Reserve 
Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).  
 
14. The aggregate amount of bids submitted by an investor in an auction should not exceed the 
notified amount of auction.   
 
Decision Making Process 
 
15. On the basis of bids received, the Reserve Bank will determine the minimum price/maximum 
yield up to which tenders for purchase of Government Security will be accepted at the 
auctions. 
  
16. Bids quoted at rates lower than the minimum price/higher than the maximum yield 
determined by the Reserve Bank of India will be rejected. 
  
17. Reserve Bank of India will have the full discretion to accept or reject any or all bids either 
wholly or partially without assigning any reason. 
 
Issue of Securities 
  
18. Issue of securities to the successful bidders will be by credit to Subsidiary General Ledger 
Account (SGL) or to Constituents’ Subsidiary General Ledger Account (CSGL), maintained 
with Reserve Bank of India. 
 
Periodicity of Interest Payment 
 
19. Interest on the Government Security will generally be paid half-yearly other than in case of 
securities with non-standard maturities. The exact periodicity of coupon payment is 
invariably mentioned in the specific notification for the issue of security. 
 
Underwriting of the Government Securities 
   
20. The underwriting of the Government Securities under auctions by the ‘Primary Dealers’ will 
be as per the “Revised Scheme of Underwriting Commitment and Liquidity Support” 
announced by the Reserve Bank vide circular RBI/2007-08/186 dated November 14, 2007 
as amended from time to time. 
 
Eligibility for Repurchase Transactions (Repo) 
  
21. The securities will be eligible for Repurchase Transactions (Repo) as per the conditions 
mentioned in Master Direction – Reserve Bank of India (Repurchase Transactions (Repo)) 
Directions, 2025 as amended from time to time. 
  
Eligibility for ‘When Issued’ Trading 
 
22. The securities will be eligible for “When Issued” trading in accordance with the guidelines on 
‘When Issued transactions in Central Government Securities’ issued by the Reserve Bank 
of India vide circular No. RBI/2018-19/25 dated July 24, 2018 as amended from time to time. 
 
Investment by Non-Residents 
 
23. Investments by Non-Residents are subject to the guidelines on ‘Fully Accessible Route’ for 
Investment by Non-residents in Government Securities and other related guidelines as 
issued by the Reserve Bank from time to time.

October 30, 2026 
 
Premature redemption under Sovereign Gold Bond (SGB) Scheme - 
Redemption Price for premature redemption of SGB 2021-22 Series VII due on 
November 02, 2026 
 
     In terms of GOI notification F.No. 4(5)-B(W&M)/2021 dated October 21, 2021 (SGB 
2021-22 Series VII - Issue date November 02, 2021) on Sovereign Gold Bond 
Scheme, premature redemption of Gold Bond may be permitted after fifth year from 
the date of issue of such Gold Bond on the date on which interest is payable. 
Accordingly, the due date of premature redemption of the above tranche shall be on 
November 02, 2026. 
 
2. Further, the redemption price of SGB shall be based on simple average of closing 
price of gold of 999 purity of previous three business days from the date of redemption, 
as published by the India Bullion and Jewellers Association Ltd (IBJA). Accordingly, 
the redemption price for premature redemption due on November 02, 2026, shall be 
₹14,167/- (Rupees Fourteen Thousand One Hundred and Sixty-Seven Only) per 
unit of SGB based on the simple average of closing price of gold for the three business 
days i.e., October 28, October 29, and October 30, 2026.

title: Lending and Deposit Rates of Scheduled Commercial Banks – October 2026
file_extracted_text:
October 30, 2026 
 
Lending and Deposit Rates of Scheduled Commercial Banks – October 2026 
 
     Data on lending and deposit rates of scheduled commercial banks (SCBs) (excluding 
regional rural banks and small finance banks) received during October 2026 are set out 
in Tables 1 to 9. 
  
Highlights:  
 
Lending Rates: 
 
• The weighted average lending rate (WALR) on outstanding rupee loans of 
SCBs remained unchanged at 8.96 per cent in September 2026 compared to 
August 2026. 
• The WALR on fresh rupee loans of SCBs declined to 8.51 per cent in 
September 2026 from 8.61 per cent in August 2026. 
• 1-Year median Marginal Cost of Funds based Lending Rate (MCLR) of SCBs 
declined to 8.55 per cent in October 2026 from 8.61 per cent in September 
2026. 
• The WALR on fresh as well as outstanding rupee loans exhibited a mixed 
movement across sectors in September 2026. 
 
Deposit Rates: 
 
• The weighted average domestic term deposit rate (WADTDR) on outstanding 
rupee term deposits of SCBs marginally declined to 6.55 per cent in September 
2026 from 6.56 per cent in August 2026. 
• The WADTDR on fresh rupee term deposits of SCBs declined to 5.61 per cent 
in September 2026 from 5.67 per cent in August 2026.

title: Sectoral Deployment of Bank Credit – September 2026
file_extracted_text:
October 30, 2026 
 
Sectoral Deployment of Bank Credit – September 2026 
     Data on sectoral deployment of bank credit for the month of September 2026, collected 
from 41 select scheduled commercial banks (SCBs), which together account for about 95 
per cent of the total non-food credit by all SCBs1, are set out in Statements I and II. 
    On a year-on-year (y-o-y) basis, non-food bank credit2 grew by 19.1 per cent as on the 
fortnight ended September 30, 2026, compared to 11.2 per cent during the corresponding 
fortnight of the previous year (i.e., October 03, 2025). 
 
Highlights of the sectoral deployment of bank credit as on the fortnight ended 
September 30, 2026, are given below: 
• 
Credit to agriculture and allied activities registered a y-o-y growth of 19.5 per cent 
vis-a-vis 8.9 per cent in the corresponding fortnight of the previous year. 
• 
Credit to industry recorded a y-o-y growth of 19.5 per cent (7.7 per cent in the 
corresponding fortnight of last year). While credit to ‘large’ and ‘medium’ industries 
grew at an accelerated pace, ‘micro and small’ industries exhibited steady growth. 
Among major industries, credit to ‘infrastructure’, ‘basic metal and metal products’, 
‘all engineering’, ‘chemical and chemical products’, ‘food processing’ and ‘textiles’ 
marked buoyant y-o-y growth.  
• 
Credit to services sector registered a y-o-y growth of 28.3 per cent (9.9 per cent in 
the corresponding fortnight of the previous year), supported by buoyant growth in 
segments such as ‘non-banking financial companies’ (NBFCs), ‘trade’ ‘commercial 
real estate’, ‘transport operators’ and ‘professional services’. 
 
 
1 Data pertain to the last reporting fortnight of the month, based on sector-wise and industry-wise bank 
credit (SIBC) return. With effect from December 31, 2025, definition of last reporting fortnight has been 
changed to the last day of the month under the Banking Laws (Amendment) Act 2025. Accordingly, the 
y-o-y growth rates from December 2025 onwards are based on end-of-month data for the current year 
and data for the last reporting fortnight (as per old definition) for the corresponding month of the previous 
year. 
2 Non-food credit data are based on Section-42 return which covers all scheduled commercial banks 
(SCBs).
